definitions.explanation: A placeholder pronoun used when referring to unspecified people or when listing names without specifying who exactly. Used like 'so-and-so' or 'Mr./Ms. X' in English.

examples.japanese: {誰々|だれだれ}さんが{来|く}るらしい。
{誰々|だれだれ}が{何|なに}を{担当|たんとう}するか{決|き}めよう。
examples.english: Let's decide who will be in charge of what.

examples.japanese: {誰々|だれだれ}と{誰々|だれだれ}が{参加|さんか}するのか{教|おし}えてください。
examples.english: Please tell me exactly who will be participating.

notes:
USAGE:
A reduplicated form of {誰|だれ}. Used as a placeholder for actual names when the speaker doesn't want to specify or doesn't know exactly who. Similar patterns exist with other question words: {何々|なになに} (such-and-such thing), {何処々々|どこどこ} (such-and-such place).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {誰々|だれだれ}さん (Mr./Ms. So-and-so)
- {誰々|だれだれ}と{誰々|だれだれ} (this person and that person)
